factCards.text: Velcro began as a walk in the Alps. George de Mestral looked at the burdock burrs clinging to his trousers under a microscope, saw tiny hooks, and spent years turning the idea into a hook-and-loop fastener patented in the 1950s.
Teflon was a mistake. In 1938 DuPont chemist Roy Plunkett opened a cylinder of a refrigerant gas and found a waxy white solid instead of gas: polytetrafluoroethylene.
factCards.sourceTitle: Science History Institute — Roy J. Plunkett

factCards.text: RADAR started life as an acronym, from radio detection and ranging, adopted by the US Navy around 1940. It has since become an ordinary noun, and a palindrome by coincidence.
